title.narrative: ARC Community Based Eco-DRR Phase 2 Resilience 2022-24 (CBED II)

description.narrative: CBED II har sin utgångspunkt i de resultat som åstadkommits under CBED I, då man lyckades förbättra naturresurser (mark, vatten och vegetation), och därigenom minska risken för översvämningar samt förbättra målsamhällenas förmåga att reagera på katastrofer. Målen för insatsen är a) att säkra att försörjning på landsbygden är bättre anpassad och mer motståndskraftig mot klimatförändringar och naturkatastrofer och b) förbättrad förvaltning och användning av naturresurser i landsbygdssamhällen. Detta ska uppnås genom ett integrerat och decentraliserat tillvägagångsätt som fokuserar på direkt stöd till de mest sårbara grupperna i de samhällen som omfattas av stödet, inklusive kvinnor, barn, äldre och människor med funktionsnedsättning.

CBED II will build on the achievements and successes from CBED I. This implemented intervention prepared the groundwork to CBED II through realizing improved the natural resources (soil, water and vegetation), reduced risk of floods and enhanced the ability of target communities to respond to disasters. The overall impact of CBED-II is that Afghanistan’s vulnerable communities and households are more resilient to and able to mitigate the impacts of climatic and economic shocks. This will be materialized through an integrated and decentralized approach which focuses on direct support to the most vulnerable populations, including women, children, elderly and people living with disabilities.

CBED II will build on the achievements and successes from CBED I. This implemented intervention prepared the groundwork to CBED II through realizing improved the natural resources (soil, water and vegetation), reduced risk of floods and enhanced the ability of target communities to respond to disasters.
The overall impact of CBED-II is that Afghanistans vulnerable communities and households are more resilient to and able to mitigate the impacts of climatic and economic shocks. The project has two inter-related outcomes, which are:
Outcome 1: Rural livelihoods are better adapted and more resilient to climate change and natural disasters.
Outcome 2: Rural communities benefit from improved stewardship and usage of natural resources.
These will be achieved through the following outputs:
Output 1: Vulnerable households are supported to strengthen food security and recover from climatic and economic shocks.
Output 2: Men and women are supported to increase production, productivity, quality, and diversity of on- and off-farm products.
Output 3: Men and women are supported to improve value addition and access to markets and services for on- and off-farm products.
Output 4: Key stakeholders gain knowledge and skills in climate adaptation.
The inter-connectivity of the impact, outcomes, intermediate outcomes, outputs, and activities are detailed in the Theory of Change.

Examples of results OUTPUT 1: VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS ARE SUPPORTED TO STRENGTHEN FOOD SECURITY AND RECOVER FROM CLIMATIC AND ECONOMIC SHOCKS Between 2022 and 2024, the project achieved remarkable cumulative progress across all output indicators. A total of 3,022 household members (2,960 male and 62 female) earned 42,335,672?AFN through cash over-for work activities that improved watershed and irrigation infrastructure in their communities, exceeding the target. In agriculture, 3,417 farmers (3,363 male and 54 female) planted autumn wheat and/or fodder crops with CBED support, also surpassing expectations. Furthermore, 1,225 women farmers established kitchen gardens for food security with CBED support, meeting the target. In poultry and animal rearing, 1,570 women received 27,295 chickens and 100 women received animal rearing support, marking an overachievement. Additionally, 445 women started bio briquettes production for winter heating, fully achieving the goal. Lastly, 123 women initiated home based nurseries with CBED support, successfully reaching the target. Overall, the cumulative results demonstrate strong success and, in several cases, overachievement particularly in income generation, agricultural productivity, and womens' empowerment.
OUTPUT 2: MEN AND WOMEN SUPPORTED TO INCREASE PRODUCTION, PRODUCTIVITY, QUALITY AND DIVERSITY OF ON AND OFF FARM PRODUCTS Between 2022 and 2024, a total of 7 participatory assessment(s) of agriculture and livestock were conducted, and 7 technical and market assessments were undertaken, meeting the targets for both indicators. In addition, 17,753 farmers (13,967 male and 3,786 female) practiced sustainable crop production and/or livestock rearing with CBED support, which overachieved the target. Training on bio fertilizers and bio pesticides production and use also exceeded expectations, reaching 12,987 farmers (12,061 male and 926 female). Training on efficient water use technologies and methods achieved the target with 11,061 farmers trained (10,533 male and 528 female). Furthermore, CBED supported the establishment of 30 Agro service centers and 25 zero energy potato storages, meeting the cumulative target. All 30 Veterinary Field Units (VFU) planned were established and/or strengthened. Finally, 4,702 farmers (2,281 male and 2,421 female) were trained on animal health, welfare and management, achieving the target for this indicator.
OUTPUT 3: MEN AND WOMEN SUPPORTED TO IMPROVE VALUE ADDITION AND ACCESS TO MARKETS AND SERVICES FOR ON AND OFF FARM PRODUCTS Between 2022 and 2024, a total of 170 men and women producer groups were established, achieving the cumulative target. In addition, 1,199 men and women producer group members were trained on economic rights and leadership, meeting the target. Training on rotating savings and loan reached 692 women producer group members (162 male and 530 female), achieving the planned result. Furthermore, 170 producer groups started post production processing and value addition activities, fully achieving the cumulative target. All 80 producer groups planned to start market linkage activities did so. Awareness sessions on economic participation from a gender perspective were conducted in 245 communities, reaching 4,360 participants (1,825 male and 2,535 female). Finally, 7 training manuals for output 3 were developed and training of trainers held, achieving the cumulative target.
OUTPUT 4: KEY STAKEHOLDERS GAIN KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS IN CLIMATE ADAPTATION Between 2022 and 2024, a total of 1,250 youth in target communities were trained or provided exposure to climate change, watershed management and climate resilient agriculture and livestock, fully achieving the cumulative target. The establishment of demonstration/model school gardens exceeded expectations, with 101 schools reached. Similarly, 101 schools received first aid kits and first aid training, meeting the cumulative goal. Training on principles of sustainable agriculture, livestock and livelihood strengthening was conducted for 6,127 Community Based Disaster Management Committees (CBDMC) and Womens Management Committees (WMC) (3,701 male and 2,426 female), over achieving the target. Training on repair and maintenance of project infrastructure and implements reached 3,969 CBDMCs and WMCs (2,434 male and 1,535 female), achieving the planned result. In addition, the project participated in 1 Global event and a number of national level meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Change to promote the CBED project and share best practices and lessons learnt, meeting the cumulative target. Finally, 11 types of communication materials were developed for knowledge sharing from the CBED project, achieving the target.
